newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Coffee supplies from Vietnam's Dak Lak hit by rain.
newsitem.headline: Coffee supplies from Vietnam's Dak Lak hit by rain.

text.p: Coffee supplies in Vietnam's main producing area, Dak Lak province, were being hit by torrential rains on Friday which some dealers said had forced local trade to a virtual halt.
"The weather's terrible. There's no coffee in Dak Lak. You can't buy a bean," said a trader in the provincial capital.
"Even a week ago there was a lot of coffee moving. We're exporting now about 100 tonnes a day, but that's coffee we bought before the rains came."
Dealers in Saigon said coffee from Dak Lak was still available and had been trading over the last week at around $1,100 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, generally unchanged from a week earlier.
"We hear these stories about the rains and that bean moisture is up, but it's not having much impact here," one said.
They said moisture levels were not significantly higher than normal but continual dampening and drying of beans by farmers was hitting quality.
Dak Lak province is responsible for up to two-thirds of Vietnam's total coffee output, which this season is expected to reach 270,000 tonnes.
